verdict.rationale: Databricks documents its own pieces for this story: governance is enforced whenever a table is queried, and Unity Catalog objects can be worked with through SQL, the CLI and REST APIs, which covers schema discovery. It also offers MCP tooling that lets an agent authenticate and query data, a REST API reference, and CLI-installed agent skills that include databricks-dbsql. What the evidence never shows is the end-to-end headless loop: executing an ad-hoc SQL statement over CLI or API and reading the result rows back. missing for 10: a documented SQL statement-execution API or CLI command that returns result sets, a concrete agent authentication flow for the CLI or API, and hands-on or independent corroboration of a dashboard-free agent SQL loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can run governed SQL end to end — authenticate, discover schemas, query, and read results back through a CLI or API with no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: You work with the objects Unity Catalog governs through Catalog Explorer, SQL, the Databricks CLI, and REST APIs.
enforcing access control when you query a table or call a model, tracking lineage as data and AI assets are used, logging activity for auditing
Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets your agent query data, search documents, and call external services.
Discover, authenticate to, and call managed, MCP Service, and custom MCP servers from your agent code
The Databricks CLI (command-line interface) allows you to interact with the Databricks platform from your local terminal or automation scripts.
